results.evidence: Section 12.2: "At the end of the Initial Subscription Term and each Renewal Term, the Subscription Term shall renew automatically for a successive renewal term of 24 months (each, a "Renewal Term"), unless either party gives the other written notice of non-renewal at least one hundred twenty (120) days before the end of the then-current Subscription Term. A non-renewal notice is effective only if it is delivered in accordance with Section 16.1 at least 120 days before the end of the then-current Subscription Term." Side Letter s.4.1: "Licensee delivered its written notice of non-renewal of the Subscription Term to Licensor on 14 October 2026."
results.reason: The Order Form sets a 1 February 2024 start and a 36-month Initial Subscription Term, so the term ends 31 January 2027. The 120-day non-renewal deadline was therefore 3 October 2026. Praidein's notice of 14 October 2026 was 11 days late. Under the strict 'effective only if' language, Praidein appears bound to a 24-month Renewal Term running to 31 January 2029, which means roughly two further years of Fees of at least US$175,200 a year, plus the Cleveland site fee. This lands while Praidein is being acquired by Ostrander. Nothing cures the problem. The Side Letter only records Zousen's position that the notice was untimely and has both parties reserve their rights. The Side Letter invoices Cleveland only to 31 January 2027, which does not concede renewal either way. Praidein has not accepted the renewal, and no renewal-period payment is recorded. The issue is therefore still live and actionable. Praidein's options include contesting the renewal, negotiating with Zousen, or factoring the exposure into the merger.

results.evidence: Licensor may assign or transfer this Order Form and the Agreement, in whole or in part, together with any of its rights and obligations under them, without Licensee's consent, to any Affiliate or to any acquirer of all or part of its business or assets. Licensor shall give Licensee written notice of the assignment or transfer within 30 days after it takes effect.
results.reason: The problem is present and still actionable for Praidein. Agreement Section 15.1 requires each party to get the other's consent before assigning. But Order Form Section 7 lets Zousen assign without consent to an Affiliate or to an acquirer of any part of its business. Agreement Section 1.3 makes the Order Form prevail over the body of the Agreement, so Section 7 controls. Zousen gives notice only after the transfer has taken effect. Zousen can also split the contract off ('in part') with a divested product line. Praidein stays bound by mutual consent under Section 15.1, and a change of control of Praidein triggers Zousen's consent right, termination and fee acceleration under Section 15.3. That matters because the Ostrander merger is pending. The Side Letter does not change Section 7: its Section 5 leaves the Order Form unmodified. Nothing shows Praidein has accepted an assignment, and the relationship is ongoing, possibly into a disputed 24-month renewal. Praidein's data (pricing, recipes, production volumes) could pass to an assignee it did not choose, so the asymmetry remains a live issue to raise.

results.evidence: Order Form Section 2.1: "For this Order Form and the Software licensed under it, "Authorized User" means a named employee of Licensee who works at an Authorized Site, who has been issued a unique user credential by Licensee's system administrator, and whom Licensee has registered in the Software's user administration console." Section 2.4: "Access to or use of the Software by any individual other than an Authorized User, and any use above the Subscription Quantity, is charged at the overage rate of US$145 per individual per month (or part of a month) during which that access or use occurs."
results.reason: The problem is present and still actionable for Praidein. The Agreement (Section 1.1) defines Authorized User broadly to include "employees, contractors and agency workers of Licensee and its Affiliates." Recital B states Licensee staffs its kitchens "largely with agency galley crews." Order Form Section 2.1 narrows the definition to named employees of Licensee, and Agreement Section 1.3 gives the Order Form precedence over the Agreement body. The Side Letter does not cure the conflict: it adds the Cleveland site and expressly leaves the Order Form "unmodified" otherwise. As a result, agency crews, contractors and Affiliate staff, including Ostrander personnel after the pending merger, fall outside the licensed users. Each such individual triggers the Licensee's obligation to pay US$145 per individual per month, and that use risks breach claims. Licensor's quarterly audit right makes the exposure real. The subscription continues, and Licensor says it has auto-renewed for 24 months, so the exposure is ongoing. Nothing in the folder shows Praidein has accepted overage charges.

results.evidence: Section 15.3: "Any Change of Control of Licensee shall be deemed an assignment of this Agreement by Licensee requiring Licensor's prior written consent under Section 15.1. ... If a Change of Control occurs without Licensor's prior written consent, Licensor may terminate this Agreement and all Order Forms on 30 days' written notice to Licensee. On that termination, all Fees for the remainder of the Subscription Term shall be accelerated and become immediately due and payable." Side Letter Recital B: "Under the Merger Agreement, Ostrander will acquire 100% of the equity interests of Licensee." Side Letter Section 5: "Except as expressly set out in this Side Letter, the Agreement and the Order Form remain unmodified and in full force and effect."
results.reason: The problem is present and still actionable. Ostrander's acquisition of 100% of Praidein's equity is a Change of Control under Section 15.3. The Side Letter records the merger but gives no consent and leaves the Agreement otherwise unmodified, so on closing Zousen may terminate on 30 days' notice and accelerate all remaining Fees. The exposure is larger because of the renewal dispute. The 36-month Initial Term ends 31 January 2027. Praidein's 14 October 2026 non-renewal notice came after the 120-day deadline (about 3 October 2026), and Zousen calls it ineffective. If Zousen is right, the Subscription Term runs a further 24 months to January 2029, and acceleration would cover that period. Both parties reserved their rights on the notice, and the merger has not yet closed. Praidein can therefore still seek Zousen's consent before closing, which Section 15.1 says may not be unreasonably withheld, or negotiate a waiver.
